title: Smooth principal localization: the localized conormal sequence of a presentation is split exact
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$, $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal and $A=P/I$; the conormal module $I/I^2$ is an $A$-module. Let $\mathrm d:I/I^2\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA\,\mathrm dx_i$ (the free $A$-module on symbols $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$) be the $A$-linear map $\mathrm d(g\bmod I^2)=\sum_{i=1}^n\overline{\partial g/\partial x_i}\,\mathrm dx_i$, with $\partial/\partial x_i$ the formal partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and the bar the image in $A$. Let $a\in A$ be such that the localization $A_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let $\mathrm d_a:(I/I^2)_a\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i$ be the localization of $\mathrm d$ at $a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then (1) $\mathrm d_a$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse (in particular it is injective); (2) the $A_a$-linear map $\pi:\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\to\Omega_{A_a/R}$, $\mathrm dx_i\mapsto\mathrm d(\bar x_i/1)$ ($\Omega_{A_a/R}$ and its derivation as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), is surjective with kernel the image of $\mathrm d_a$. Hence $0\to(I/I^2)_a\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_a}\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i\xrightarrow{\pi}\Omega_{A_a/R}\to0$ is a split short exact sequence and $(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong A_a^{\oplus n}$ as $A_a$-modules.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard), part (e), first sentence ('By assumption we have a short exact sequence 0 -> (I/I^2)_a -> (+) A_a dx_i -> Omega_{A_a/R} -> 0 which is split exact'); the same argument in the proof of Lemma Tag 07C6 (lemma-find-strictly-standard, lines 160-170). It rests on Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy: the naive cotangent complex of any presentation is homotopy equivalent to NL_{A/R}), Lemma Tag 00S7 (lemma-localize-NL), Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL) and Definition Tag 00T2 (definition-smooth)

proof.text: Let P be the quotient presentation R[x_1,...,x_n] -> A and let Q be the presentation of B=A_a obtained by adjoining the generator 1/a. The polynomial ring of Q is formally smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]. Since B is smooth, its first cotangent homology vanishes by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Mathlib Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex_injective_iff therefore makes the differential of Q injective. Apply the injectivity equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent], with the lift P.sigma(a), to deduce injectivity of the B-base change of the conormal differential of P.

source.place: Definition Tag 00T2 and Lemma Tag 08JZ; Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Basic, Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex_injective_iff

proof.text: Identify the cotangent module of the quotient presentation P with I/I^2 using Algebra.Extension.cotangentEquivCotangentKer and Ideal.Cotangent.equivOfEq; the equality of ideals is ker(P -> A)=I. Extend this equivalence from the polynomial ring to A using surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor], localizing this conormal module gives B tensor_A P.Cotangent. The base change of the polynomial differential basis of [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] identifies B tensor_A P.CotangentSpace with B^n. Define d by conjugating the base-changed differential with these equivalences; it is injective by step 1. On g mod I^2 divided by one, the localization equivalence gives 1 tensor (g mod I^2), the differential gives 1 tensor dg, and its i-th basis coordinate is the image of partial_i g. This proves precisely the specified coordinate formula.

The quotient conormal sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] is right exact; in Mathlib it is P.toExtension.exact_cotangentComplex_toKaehler with toKaehler_surjective. Tensor it with B over A; [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] preserves exactness and surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], B tensor_A Omega_{A/R} is canonically Omega_{B/R}; use KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale, since A -> B is a localization. Define pi by conjugating the base-changed quotient map with this equivalence and the basis equivalence of step 2. Its value on dx_i is d(x_i/1), by Generators.toKaehler_cotangentSpaceBasis and KaehlerDifferential.map_D. Conjugation preserves exactness and surjectivity, so ker pi = range d.

Smoothness of B makes Omega_{B/R} projective by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Apply the lifting property of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to its identity and the surjective map pi to obtain a linear section s with pi composed with s equal to the identity. For an injective d and exact pair (d,pi), Function.Exact.splitSurjectiveEquiv gives e:B^n -> (I/I^2)_a times Omega_{B/R}, with d=e^{-1} composed with the first inclusion. Thus l=first projection composed with e satisfies l composed with d=id, and e^{-1} is the requested product equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_localization_conormal_split [Smooth R B] : ∃ (d : M →ₗ[B] (Fin n → B)) (π : (Fin n → B) →ₗ[B] KaehlerDifferential R B), (∀ (g : I) (i : Fin n), d (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers a) I.Cotangent (I.toCotangent g)) i = algebraMap A B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.pderiv i (g : _)))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, π (Pi.single i 1) = KaehlerDifferential.D R B (algebraMap A B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (MvPolynomial.X i)))) ∧ (∃ l : (Fin n → B) →ₗ[B] M, l.comp d = LinearMap.id) ∧ Function.Injective d ∧ Function.Surjective π ∧ LinearMap.ker π = LinearMap.range d ∧ (∃ s : KaehlerDifferential R B →ₗ[B] (Fin n → B), π.comp s = LinearMap.id) ∧ Nonempty ((M × KaehlerDifferential R B) ≃ₗ[B] (Fin n → B))
lean.note: R, n, I, a are explicitly bound section variables. Local notation A = MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ I, B = Localization.Away a, M = LocalizedModule.Away a I.Cotangent. The maps are existentially specified by their uniquely determining generator values; no arbitrary map hypothesis is imposed.
